findings.summary: Rewritten from() no longer copies the original error's own properties, so Node fields like errno, syscall, address and port are lost.
from() throws a TypeError when error is null or undefined, which can happen since fetch.js:257 passes err && err.code.
The old default message 'Error' in from() is gone.
cause is now enumerable, whereas the old code made it non-enumerable on purpose to avoid JSON noise.
`code || error.code` replaces `code == null ? error.code : code`, so an explicit falsy code now loses to error.code.
status is now undefined instead of null when the response has no status.
isAxiosError is now an own enumerable property instead of a non-enumerable prototype one, so it shows up in spreads, Object.keys and equality checks.

__CANCEL__ is now an own enumerable instance property instead of a prototype one, with the same side effects as isAxiosError. Objects built with Object.create(CanceledError.prototype) are no longer recognized by isCancel.
The new isNativeError tests use require inside ESM specs and skip silently outside Node. Nothing covers the from() regressions.
